title: Reservation lifecycle, observability, and decisioning PRD
creator: Sophie Chen
summary: Introduce a reservation lifecycle and decisioning surface plus comprehensive observability for reserved capacity so operators can understand, simulate, and tune autoscale, burst, and isolation behaviors without guessing. This PRD defines the data model, UI, APIs, success metrics and rollout plan.
problem_statement: Operators lack a single source of truth for reserved-pool state transitions, autoscale decisions, burst admissions, and tenant eviction events. Root-cause analysis requires stitching logs from multiple systems, and rollouts of guardrail changes are high-risk because there is no safe simulation or replay surface. This leads to suboptimal headroom, unexpected tenant contention, and slow incident resolution.
goals_and_success_metrics: Provide a reservation lifecycle model that records create/modify/scale/evict/release events with immutable audit entries.
Expose a dashboard showing live headroom, utilization, admission rate, 95th percentile latency and queue lengths per-reservation and per-tenant.
Create a decisioning API that surfaces why an autoscale or eviction decision occurred (inputs, thresholds, feature flags) with decision latency <= 200ms.
Enable a simulator (what-if) that can replay 72 hours of traffic against proposed autoscale and burst policies in under 30 minutes for a single reservation.

Success metrics: Mean time to detect reservation saturation reduced by 3x within 4 weeks of launch; incident postmortem time related to reserved capacity decisions reduced by 50% in two quarters; 90% of policy rollouts performed via canary/simulate before prod flip.
Telemetry retention: primary time-series retained 90 days; detailed decision logs retained 365 days for compliance customers.
non_goals: Replace core scheduling runtime — this project surfaces decisions and records lifecycle events but does not implement new kernel-level scheduling optimizations.
Full multi-cluster migration tooling — cross-region reservation migration is out of scope for initial launch.
End-to-end billing integration — billing hooks will be added in a follow-up.
user_personas: Platform Engineer: responsible for capacity contracts and tuning autoscale/eviction policy parameters.
Support Engineer/Oncall: needs quick root-cause signals and an audit trail during incidents.
Product Manager / Customer Success: reviews utilization and SLO compliance for enterprise customers.
Customer Admin: for Private/Dedicated customers with visibility into their own reservations and audit logs.
scope_in: Event schema for reservation lifecycle (create, update, scale, preempt, evict, release) with immutable timestamps and reason codes.
Decisioning API that returns decision_id, inputs snapshot, matched rule, and ranked reasons.
Reservation dashboard in Console with filters for pool, tenant, zone, and time window plus critical alerts and exportable CSVs.
Simulation sandbox that replays stored telemetry with configurable policy knobs and reports delta estimates for latency, cost, and headroom.
Audit log streaming to customer Kinesis/SQS/S3 (configurable) and internal retention controls for enterprise plans.
Backend telemetry (prometheus metrics, traces) and standardized labels to support SLOs and alerts.
scope_out: Dynamic physical rebalancing of GPU allocations across zones.
Automated billing reconciliation and invoicing changes.
Per-request semantic quality monitoring (LLM output diffs) — quality monitoring remains separate.
requirements: REQ-001: Event model: every reservation lifecycle change must emit a single JSON event with fields: reservation_id, tenant_id, pool_id, operator_id, event_type, reason_code, previous_state, new_state, timestamp, correlated_decision_id (optional).

REQ-002: Decisioning API: POST /decision/explain accepts reservation_id and decision_id and returns a human-readable rationale, numeric inputs snapshot, and a link to the related audit event. The API must respond within 200ms 95% of the time.

REQ-003: Dashboard: Console must show per-reservation: current_allocated_gpus, headroom_gpus, 1/5/95 percentile latency, queue_depth, admission_rate, and recent decision events; filters and CSV export available.

REQ-004: Simulator: ingest 72h of compacted telemetry in <30min and produce a simulation report comparing baseline vs candidate policy in terms of token-cost delta, estimated latency delta, and % of requests preempted.

REQ-005: Telemetry: emit time-series metrics for reservation_utilization, admission_rate, preemption_rate, decision_latency, and headroom over time with 10s granularity; retain primary series for 90 days.
REQ-006: Audit: append-only audit log per-reservation with event immutability guarantee and export endpoint; exportable to S3/Kinesis with encryption at rest.
REQ-007: RBAC: Console views must respect tenant isolation - customer admins see only their reservations; internal users see cross-tenant dashboard per role policy.
REQ-008: Canary rollout: ability to enable a new policy for a configurable small percentage of traffic (0.1% - 10%) with automatic rollback trigger on defined anomalies.
user_stories: AS a Platform Engineer, I WANT to see why a reservation scaled down during business hours SO THAT I can decide if the autoscale threshold needs tuning.
AS a Support Engineer, I WANT to query decision_id 12345 and get the inputs and rule match SO THAT I can explain to the customer what happened within an incident timeline.
AS a Customer Admin, I WANT the audit log for my reservation for the last 180 days SO THAT I can satisfy audit requests.
AS a PM, I WANT to run a what-if simulation of a more aggressive burst policy SO THAT I can quantify cost vs latency tradeoffs before rollout.
acceptance_criteria: AC-001: All reservation lifecycle state changes are recorded and visible in Console within 30s of occurrence for 95% of events.
AC-002: Decisioning API returns a human-readable rationale and an inputs snapshot and meets 200ms 95th percentile latency in perf testing at projected QPS.
AC-003: Dashboard displays the required metrics and can filter by tenant/pool/time window; exported CSV contains the same columns visible in UI.

AC-004: Simulator can complete a 72h replay against a single reservation in <30 minutes in the staging environment using representative telemetry and produces a delta report with cost and latency columns.
AC-005: Telemetry metrics are emitted with 10s granularity and appear in the alerting pipeline; an alert fires when reservation_utilization > 95% for >5 minutes.
AC-006: Audit export to S3/Kinesis is verified end-to-end with encryption and correct partitioning keys for tenant/reservation.
AC-007: RBAC tests confirm customer admins cannot view other tenants' reservations and internal role mapping is enforced.
AC-008: Canary rollouts can be configured and, when anomaly thresholds trigger, policies auto-rollback and generate an incident ticket with decision logs attached.
data_and_telemetry: Core metrics: reservation_utilization, allocated_gpus, headroom_gpus, admission_rate, preemption_rate, decision_latency, queue_depth.
Decision logs: decision_id, timestamp, policy_version, inputs_snapshot (numerical), matched_rule_id, score, confidence, correlated_event_ids.
Retention: metrics 90 days, decision logs 365 days for enterprise customers; compressed archives exported to long-term S3 bucket monthly.
Tracing: span for decision path must include correlation id and be linkable to the request trace in the runtime (trace_id).
ui_changes: New Console page: Reservations -> Lifecycle (table + timeline view).
Reservation detail panel: live headroom graph, recent decision events, audit timeline, 'simulate policy' button, and 'export audit' action.
Canary controls: simple slider to set percent of traffic and anomaly thresholds with immediate preview of expected traffic split.
Notification templates for auto-rollback events and policy-change approvals.
api_contracts: GET /api/v1/reservations/{id}/audit?start=&end=&page= -> paginated list of event_ids and timestamps; supports export token generation.
POST /api/v1/reservations/{id}/simulate -> {policy_payload} returns simulation_report_id. Poll GET /api/v1/simulations/{id} for results.
Event sink contract: publish reservation events to internal event bus with pre-defined schema and partition key = tenant_id.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement event model, basic dashboard, and decisioning API behind feature flag. Duration: 4 weeks.
Phase 2 (internal canary): enable for 10% internal traffic, validate decision latency and simulator performance. Duration: 3 weeks.
Phase 3 (external beta): invite 3 enterprise customers to opt-in, enable audit exports and extended retention. Duration: 4 weeks.
Phase 4 (GA): full public rollout with default telemetry retention and console exposure. Monitor success metrics for 8 weeks before marking done.
dependencies: ENG-21012: unified-event-pipeline (delivery of append-only event bus).
ENG-22350: console-dashboard-framework (widgets and CSV export components).
PM-712459: KMS integration for audit export encryption (coordination).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Decisioning API adds latency to request flow if used synchronously. Mitigation: make it async/side-channel; keep synchronous only for admin debugging and simulation.
Risk: Large decision log retention increases storage costs. Mitigation: tiered retention with compression and customer-configurable retention; default conservative retention.
Risk: Customers may misinterpret simulation output. Mitigation: include clear assumptions, confidence intervals, and 'known-unknowns' section in simulation report.
open_questions: Q1: What is the canonical list of reason_codes and matched_rule_ids we want to expose initially? (security/ops to define)
Q2: Should the decisioning API include raw numeric inputs in payload or only a url to secured snapshot? (privacy/compliance tradeoff)
Q3: What SLA do we offer for audit export delivery to customer S3 (best-effort vs guaranteed)?
